card.band: 8 h. Locating the regression is feasible for a frontier agent, but going beyond the baseline needs kernel work. A weaker model fixes only the obvious cause. Buckets by prompt and generation, quant type and thread count.
card.cheat: Lowering precision or skipping layers. The logit tolerance and top-1 equality gate closes this.
card.grading: The wall-clock median of the bench over fixed prompts and thread counts is compared to the baseline. A hard gate requires logits within a set tolerance of the baseline's, and the top-1 tokens must match. The reward is 2^u-1 against the reference's speedup.
card.reference: The upstream fix and follow-up commits, which give a measured speedup. The exact figure is not found in the row and is measured when the bundle is built. The issue's affected platform must be confirmed as CPU.
card.source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/18258 (pinned at the build before the fix), MIT
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of the regressed ggml CPU path and a small quantised model. The agent finds the cause of the throughput drop and improves token generation and prompt-processing speed on 8 cores. The delivery is the buildable tree and the bench binary.
card.title: Recover a CPU inference throughput regression in llama.cpp

spike_plan.kill_if: No CPU slowdown above 10% across the range, or the only slowdown is GPU or argument-handling code (as the cited issue is).
spike_plan.pass_if: A reproducible CPU slowdown above 10% with a first bad commit that touches the CPU path and has a measurable fix.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone llama.cpp at b7406 and at the seed commit 4a45de4f; build both CPU-only (-DGGML_CUDA=OFF) with -j 8.
Pick one small quantised model (the one shipped in the seed) and run the bench at 1, 4 and 8 threads, prompt and generation, 5 repeats each, medians.
If the CPU medians differ by less than 10% across b7406 and HEAD, stop: no CPU regression exists.
If a slowdown above 10% appears, bisect between the two commits on the CPU-only build to find the first bad commit.
Check the first bad commit's diff: does it touch ggml-cpu kernels, or only GPU layer/argument code?
Check determinism: repeat the bench 3 times; medians must agree within about 3%.

v1.summary: The seed's premise fails: issue #18258 and its fix PR #18266 concern a CUDA/GPU regression and GPU-layer argument handling, not the CPU ggml path, and no measured reference speedup is public. The repo is real and MIT-licensed and the smoke build is green, but the task would need a new CPU regression to be found first, so the card is killed as K2 unless a CPU-specific regression is established in the spike.
